item.title: Pathway blocked for wheelchair users, 16th September
item.description:
I am making this report regarding an ongoing issue with bins being left on the pavement following bin collection days My mother is a wheelchair user and needs to use the pavement to access our property. On bin collection days, the bins are regularly left on the pavement and, when they are not collected, they remain there for several days. This can make it difficult or impossible for my mother to safely pass in her wheelchair. I have spoken to my neighbour about the issue. She explained that she places the bins on the pavement because when she leaves them on the grass or within the property boundary, the bin collection drivers have previously failed to collect them, stating that the bins were not presented correctly. She has also explained that when a collection is missed, she has to report it and leave the bins outside because she is not given a specific time or date for when the missed collection will be completed. If she moves the bins back onto her property, there is a risk that they will not be collected when the council eventually returns. I understand why my neighbour is presenting the bins in this way, and she has apologised for the obstruction. However, the situation is causing an ongoing accessibility problem for my mother, and I am having to assist her in getting around the bins on collection days and for several days afterwards. I would therefore ask the council to investigate both issues together: the accessibility obstruction caused by the uncollected bins and the underlying problem of bins not being collected when they are presented from the property boundary. A practical solution is needed so that the bins can be collected reliably without obstructing the pavement and preventing wheelchair access.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 112, Ravensbury Road, St Mary Cray, Orpington, Greater London

item.title: Excessive Leaf Build-up, 16th September
item.description:
There is a constant excessive amount of leaves that builds up here! I have complained about this before - a guy came out removed some and not seen since. Why is this not cleared regularly? You can never make out the curb as it is completely covered - this is without a doubt a health and safety issue, especially with the wet weather we have been having. Can this please be fully cleared and something that is maintained. Furthermore, whomever it is that attends; can you please ensure that they do not continously shout to their colleague, "this is ridiculous, they're (Southwark Council) are lucky I'm even in" with persistent swearing. It's completely uncalled for. Best,
